# Preservation Letter (Litigation Hold Notice to an Outside Party)

## When to use this

Send this the moment the Kingdom reasonably anticipates a dispute with an outside
party, and before it has decided whether to pursue anything. It goes to the party
the Kingdom may end up opposing, or to a third party who holds material the
Kingdom will need — a platform, a contractor, a former vendor, a municipality, an
insurer, a bank.

It is the cheapest instrument in this library and the one most often sent too
late. It costs a postage stamp, takes twenty minutes, and its entire function is to
stop the ordinary machinery of deletion before it eats the evidence. Camera systems
overwrite on a fourteen-day loop. Mail retention rules purge at ninety days.
Messaging applications delete on a timer by default. Phones are traded in at
upgrade. None of that is anybody's misconduct, and all of it is irreversible.

Send it when: the Kingdom discovers an infringement it may pursue; a member or
former officer threatens suit; someone is injured on the Kingdom's premises; a
subpoena or agency inquiry arrives; a contract dispute becomes serious; or an
internal complaint of misconduct is made. Send it in the same hour the Kingdom
issues its own internal hold, never later.

Do not send it as a substitute for a demand letter, and do not send it as a threat.
It is a notice, and its tone should be flat.

## Before you send

- [ ] **The Kingdom's own legal hold has issued first,** to every internal
      custodian, per `05-EVIDENCE-AND-CHAIN-OF-CUSTODY` § 9. Sending this letter
      fixes the Kingdom's preservation duty at least as firmly as the recipient's,
      and an opponent who discovers that the Kingdom sent a preservation demand
      while its own retention rules were still deleting will make that the story.
- [ ] **The anticipated dispute can be stated in two or three sentences** —
      subject matter, the parties, the approximate period. Vague letters preserve
      nothing, because the recipient cannot tell what to keep, and a demand to
      "preserve everything" is treated as unreasonable and ignored.
- [ ] **The categories are specific to this matter,** drawn from the general list
      below and cut down to what plausibly exists. A category list copied wholesale
      from a template signals that nobody thought about it.
- [ ] **The custodians are named where they are known** — the individuals, the
      departments, the systems.
- [ ] **The relevant date range is stated,** with an opening date and, ordinarily,
      no closing date.
- [ ] **The recipient is correctly identified** as a legal entity with a registered
      agent, and a delivery method is chosen that produces proof of receipt.
      Certified mail with return receipt, plus email. The date of receipt is the
      fact this letter exists to establish.
- [ ] **The letter has been checked against `01-LEGAL-POSTURE` § 4.** It must not
      be captioned, numbered, sealed, or worded as though it were a subpoena, an
      order, or process of any kind. It is a letter from a party. That distinction
      is not cosmetic — see the Notes.
- [ ] **The matter is open in the Enforcement Docket** and a copy of the letter,
      the delivery receipt, and any acknowledgement will be deposited in the
      Evidence Vault.

## The letter

```
[APEX KINGDOM LETTERHEAD — name, postal address, telephone, email]

[DATE]

VIA CERTIFIED MAIL, RETURN RECEIPT REQUESTED, AND BY EMAIL TO [ADDRESS]

[RECIPIENT LEGAL NAME]
[ATTN: NAMED INDIVIDUAL, GENERAL COUNSEL, OR REGISTERED AGENT]
[STREET ADDRESS]
[CITY, STATE, ZIP]

Re:  Notice to preserve documents and electronically stored information
     [SUBJECT MATTER — e.g., "Use of Apex Kingdom materials at
     [URL]" / "Incident at [ADDRESS] on [DATE]"]
     Our reference: [MATTER REFERENCE]

Dear [MR./MS./MX. SURNAME]:

Apex Kingdom ("the Kingdom") anticipates that a dispute may arise concerning
[STATE THE SUBJECT MATTER IN TWO OR THREE SENTENCES — e.g., "the
reproduction of the Kingdom's copyrighted materials on the website at [URL]
between [DATE] and the present" / "the injury sustained by [NAME] at
[LOCATION] on [DATE]" / "performance of the agreement between the Kingdom
and [ENTITY] dated [DATE]"].

The purpose of this letter is to ask you to preserve material relevant to
that matter. It makes no demand for money and asserts no claim against you;
[FOR A THIRD PARTY, SUBSTITUTE: the Kingdom understands that you are not a
party to the underlying dispute, and this letter is not directed at your
conduct.] It is sent now because material of this kind is routinely lost to
ordinary retention and deletion practices before anyone turns their mind to
it.

THE OBLIGATION

Under the law of this jurisdiction, a party's obligation to preserve
evidence arises when it has notice that the evidence is relevant to
litigation, or when it should have known that the evidence may be relevant
to litigation reasonably anticipated. When that obligation attaches, routine
document retention and destruction practices must be suspended as to the
material in question. This letter is written notice for that purpose, and
the obligation attaches on your receipt of it.

WHAT SHOULD BE PRESERVED

Please preserve all documents, communications, records, data, and physical
items relating to [SUBJECT MATTER], created or received between [START DATE]
and the present, including but not limited to:

  1.  Email, including sent items, drafts, deleted items, attachments, and
      complete message headers;

  2.  Text messages, SMS, MMS, iMessage, WhatsApp, Signal, and any other
      messaging application, including group conversations and any messages
      set to delete automatically;

  3.  Messages and files in workplace collaboration systems, including
      Slack, Microsoft Teams, and any direct messages within them;

  4.  Social media posts, comments, direct messages, stories, and account
      activity records, including material posted and subsequently removed;

  5.  Documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and their drafts and revision
      histories, in native format with metadata intact;

  6.  Files held in cloud storage, including Google Drive, Dropbox,
      OneDrive, iCloud, and any shared workspace;

  7.  Website content, page source, content management system revision
      histories, server logs, access logs, and web analytics data;

  8.  Financial records: invoices, receipts, sales and donation records,
      payment processor records, bank statements, and accounting entries
      relating to [SUBJECT MATTER];

  9.  Photographs, video, and audio recordings, including security or
      surveillance footage and any recording held on a system that
      overwrites on a cycle;

  10. Voicemail, call logs, and calendar entries;

  11. Notes, diaries, and handwritten records;

  12. Contracts, correspondence with third parties, and internal memoranda
      relating to [SUBJECT MATTER];

  13. [MATTER-SPECIFIC ITEMS — e.g., "the design files and source materials
      from which the artwork at [URL] was produced" / "the physical item
      identified as [DESCRIPTION], in the condition it is now in, without
      repair, alteration, or disposal"]; and

  14. The devices and accounts on which any of the foregoing is stored.

[WHERE CUSTODIANS ARE KNOWN: The Kingdom understands that the following
individuals are likely to hold relevant material: [NAMES AND ROLES]. This
list is not exhaustive.]

WHAT THIS REQUIRES IN PRACTICE

  (a) Suspend, immediately, any automatic deletion, archiving, overwriting,
      or retention rule that would remove material within the categories
      above — including email retention rules, recycling of backup media,
      surveillance recording loops, and disappearing-message settings;

  (b) Do not delete, alter, edit, reorganize, or overwrite any such
      material;

  (c) Do not wipe, reset, reimage, sell, trade in, or dispose of any device
      or account holding such material;

  (d) Preserve material in its native format with its metadata intact. A
      printout or screenshot is not a substitute for the underlying file;

  (e) Notify the individuals who hold or control such material of this
      request; and

  (f) If material within these categories has already been lost or deleted,
      identify what it was, when it was lost, and how, so that the parties
      can address it now rather than later.

CONSEQUENCES OF FAILING TO PRESERVE

The Kingdom raises this without any suggestion that you would do otherwise.
Where evidence that should have been preserved is lost, a court may impose
measures to cure the resulting prejudice; where electronically stored
information is lost because reasonable steps were not taken to preserve it
and it cannot be restored or replaced, Rule 37(e) of the Federal Rules of
Civil Procedure permits such measures, and, on a finding that a party acted
with the intent to deprive another party of the information, permits the
court to presume the information was unfavorable, to instruct a jury that it
may or must so presume, to dismiss the action, or to enter a default
judgment. Connecticut courts likewise permit an adverse inference from the
intentional destruction of evidence and recognize intentional spoliation as
an independent tort.

ACKNOWLEDGEMENT

Please confirm in writing by [DATE — ordinarily 10 to 14 days] that you have
received this letter and have taken the steps described above. If any
category is unclear, or if compliance with any of it presents a practical
difficulty, contact me and the Kingdom will work with you to resolve it.

If you are represented in this matter, please have your attorney contact me
and I will correspond with them from that point.

Nothing in this letter waives or limits any right, claim, or remedy
available to the Kingdom, all of which are expressly reserved.

Sincerely,

______________________________
[FULL NAME]
[OFFICE HELD], Apex Kingdom
[ADDRESS] · [TELEPHONE] · [EMAIL]

[WHERE THE SIGNING OFFICER IS NOT AN ATTORNEY: I am an officer of Apex
Kingdom and am not an attorney. This letter is a request made by the Kingdom
in its own behalf.]
```

## Notes

**This letter is cheap, and that is the whole argument for sending it.** It costs
twenty minutes and a certified mailing. It requires no decision about whether to
pursue the matter, no assessment of the merits, and no lawyer. There is no cost to
a preservation letter that turns out to have been unnecessary, and no recovery from
one sent a month late. Send it first, decide afterwards. The order matters:
`05-EVIDENCE-AND-CHAIN-OF-CUSTODY` § 10 puts the hold at step six of the first
hour, before any assessment of the merits, for exactly this reason.

**Its real function is to stop the opponent's ordinary destruction cycle.** Most
lost evidence is lost innocently, by machinery nobody was watching. An organisation
with a ninety-day mail purge, a fourteen-day camera loop, and disappearing messages
turned on by default is destroying the record every day without a single person
deciding to. This letter forces someone on the other side to walk over to those
systems and switch them off. Whether they later fight the Kingdom on the merits is
a separate question; almost nobody refuses to preserve, because refusing is
indefensible and preserving is nearly free.

**And it converts innocent loss into culpable loss.** Before the letter, material
that vanishes on a retention schedule is an accident. After it, the recipient has
written notice, delivered on a tracked and dated mailing, and the same loss is
measured against Fed. R. Civ. P. 37(e) — reasonable steps, prejudice, and, at the
severe end, intent to deprive. The date of receipt is therefore the single most
valuable fact this letter produces, which is why it goes certified with a return
receipt and why the receipt is deposited in the Evidence Vault with the letter
itself. In the Second Circuit the duty attaches when a party has notice that the
evidence is relevant to litigation (*Kronisch v. United States*, 150 F.3d 112 (2d
Cir. 1998)), and the obligation to suspend routine retention and issue a hold on
reasonable anticipation of litigation was set out in *Zubulake v. UBS Warburg LLC*,
220 F.R.D. 212 (S.D.N.Y. 2003). Connecticut permits an adverse inference from
intentional destruction (*Beers v. Bayliner Marine Corp.*, 236 Conn. 769 (1996))
and recognises intentional spoliation as an independent tort (*Rizzuto v. Davidson
Ladders, Inc.*, 280 Conn. 225 (2007)).

**It is a request, not process, and the drafting protects that distinction
deliberately.** This is the template in the library that could most easily be
dressed up into something it must never be. A preservation letter that carries a
caption, a docket-style number, a seal, a signature block implying law enforcement,
a warning of "penalties" for non-compliance, or the word "ORDER" or "DEMAND" at the
head of it is a document imitating court process directed at a non-consenting
outsider, and `01-LEGAL-POSTURE` § 4 forecloses it absolutely. The Kingdom has no
power to compel preservation. What it has is the ability to give notice, and notice
is what produces the legal consequence. The template therefore says "please
preserve", offers to discuss difficulties, and states the consequences of
destruction as a description of what a court may do — not as something the Kingdom
threatens to do. That is both the honest formulation and the more effective one:
general counsel on the other side reads it, recognises it as competent, and
complies.

**Compulsion, when it becomes necessary, comes from a court and only from a
court.** Once suit is filed, material held by a non-party is obtained by subpoena
under Fed. R. Civ. P. 45 — issued by the court, served under its authority, and
enforceable by it. Pre-suit compulsion is very limited; Fed. R. Civ. P. 27 permits
a petition to perpetuate testimony only in narrow circumstances. Until then this
letter is the whole of the Kingdom's leverage, and it is more than it looks.

**Third parties are different from opponents, and the letter should say so.** A
third party ordinarily owes the Kingdom no independent duty to preserve absent a
subpoena. But most will preserve on request, because it is easy and because the
alternative is being drawn into someone else's dispute later. Say expressly that
the letter is not directed at their conduct and makes no claim against them, name a
person to call, and offer to make it easy. Platforms in particular respond to a
narrow, specific, dated request for defined account records far better than to a
broad one. Where the material is critical and the third party is unresponsive, note
that platform data retention windows are often short, and take advice about
accelerating to a filed action.

**Reissue and release.** A hold sent once is forgotten within a quarter. Where a
matter is live for months, send a short reminder. When the matter ends, release the
hold in writing, with the date, the reason, and the officer releasing it — for
outside parties as well as internal custodians. An undocumented release looks
identical to an unauthorised deletion.

---

*This is an operating template prepared to organise the Kingdom's affairs. It is
not legal advice and no attorney-client relationship arises from it. Preservation
obligations, sanctions, and the rules governing spoliation differ between federal
and Connecticut practice and turn on the particular facts and the stage of the
matter. Engage licensed Connecticut counsel before acting on any of it.*
